## Findings
- claim-1: The project documentation records the stronger statement \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) only as suspected, and says that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: Let \(q=n-r\), assume \(a=1,b=2\), and use the accepted integral Schur/Pieri presentation \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\). Then \(i,j\ge2\), \(q-i,r-j\ge1\), \(\min(i,j)=2\), and \(\min(q-i,r-j)=1\).
- claim-3: Put \[ x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}, \] \[ y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\quad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}. \] In \(Q\), Pieri relations give \[ \bar x_1+\bar y_1=0,\qquad \bar u+\bar x_2+\bar z=0,\qquad \bar u+\bar z+\bar y_2=0, \] where \(u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\) is interpreted as \(0\) if outside the \(q^r\)-box and \(z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)}\). Hence \[ \bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\qquad \bar y_2=\bar x_2. \]
- claim-4: Consequently the two \(a=1,b=2\) proposed families \[ F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2) \] have images related in \(Q\) by the unimodular diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\). Thus either family is an integral basis of its span in \(Q\) exactly when the other is.
- claim-5: **Uniform \(a=1,b=2\) elimination lemma.** In the accepted integral presentation of \(Q\), all Schur columns other than \(x_0,x_1,x_2\) admit integral unit-pivot elimination, with no residual relation on these three columns. Equivalently, \[ Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2. \]
## Strategy
Put \(d=ij\). Work degreewise in the accepted integral Schur/Pieri presentation of \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\).

For \(a=1,b=2\), the degree-\(d\) block is \(\mathbb Z\bar x_0\), and the degree-\(d+1\) block has relation
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
\]
hence is \(\mathbb Z\bar x_1\), with \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\).

In degree \(d+2\), the Schur columns are \(u,x_2,z,y_2,w\), omitting \(u\) or \(w\) when outside the box. The relevant Pieri rows are
\[
u+x_2+z,\qquad u+z+y_2,\qquad z+y_2+w.
\]
At least one of \(u,w\) is absent since
\[
\min(q-i,r-j)=1.
\]
If \(u=0\), these rows eliminate \(z,y_2\) and, if present, \(w\), leaving freely \(\bar x_2\). If \(w=0\), they eliminate \(z,y_2,u\), again leaving freely \(\bar x_2\). Thus the degree-\(d+2\) block is \(\mathbb Z\bar x_2\), and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).

Hence the three displayed degrees certify integral independence of
\[
(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\bar x_2),
\]
and the corresponding low-degree classes of \(F_2\) differ by
\(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\).

A global elimination lemma would require a degree-compatible ordering of every remaining Schur column and unit-pivot Pieri eliminations, together with an integral proof that all Pieri rows lie in the resulting selected row lattice.

## Gaps
- No uniform elimination order, termination proof, or boundary-compatible pivot construction is supplied.
- The low-degree calculation does not eliminate higher-degree columns.
- No saturation/unimodular-minor argument excludes higher-degree torsion or residual relations.
- Therefore
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2
\]
remains conjectural.
- Minimality also remains unresolved until integral basis status in all of \(Q\), and generation of \(J_v\) by the chosen family, are established.

## Next
- Define an explicit elimination order, separately auditing \(q-i=1\), \(r-j=1\), and their intersection.
- Prove each proposed pivot is a coefficient-\(1\) Pieri entry with only previously eliminated complementary terms.
- Exhibit a unimodular complementary minor, or integral reconstruction of every Pieri row from selected pivot rows, to prove saturation.
- Apply graded Nakayama only after the resulting quotient is proved integrally free of rank \(3\).
